target.title: feat: nameplate attention --wait blocks until the human acknowledges
target.body:
## Summary

`nameplate attention` gains `--wait`: the CLI blocks until the card is clicked (exit 0), auto-dismissed (exit 3), or a timeout elapses (exit 4, default 600 s, `--timeout <s>`). Without the flag, behavior is unchanged.

## Why this matters

The README's own example is an agent needing 1Password approval — but the current handoff is fire-and-forget, so the agent that raised the alert never learns whether the human showed up. With `--wait` the alert becomes a handshake the agent can branch on: proceed on 0, escalate on 3/4. The bundled agent skill (`skills/nameplate-attention`) is updated so agents adopt the flag.

## Demo

Simulated demo:

![demo](https://files.catbox.moe/csmosn.gif)

## Changes

- The ack channel mirrors the existing request handoff: a new `AttentionAck` core type writes per-request-ID files (`attention-ack-<id>.json`) next to `attention.json` and posts a `…attention.ack` Darwin notification; the CLI listens and polls the file as fallback (Darwin notifications aren't queued — same defensive pattern as the cold-launch double-post).
- Acks are per-ID rather than a single file so overlapping waiters can't consume each other's outcome; when a new request displaces an unconsumed one, the CLI writes a best-effort `superseded` ack for the displaced ID, and stale ack files are swept on wait start. Supersession in the app is keyed on the active request ID, not card presence, so headless display states still acknowledge.
- `AttentionRequest` gains an optional `id` — old app + new CLI (and vice versa) stay compatible; requests without ids never produce acks.

Known limitation: two `attention --wait` calls racing from separate processes can still last-write-wins on `attention.json` itself, in which case the displaced waiter exits at its timeout rather than promptly. Request-side queueing is being handled separately in #13, and the ack channel here will compose with it.

## Testing

`swift build` and `swift test` pass (32 tests; new `AttentionAck` suite covers round-trip, per-ID isolation, stale-file pruning, and requests without ids). Also exercised live against a local build: `--wait --duration 5` returned exit 3 with `attention outcome: autoDismissed`, and a sticky `--wait --timeout 6` returned exit 4 after the cap.
